slot_note: FC25 seed (status.py task154): the world (a bank research desk's call on a statistics office's advance real GDP print when the trade and stocks report feeding three of its lines landed late), the decision (one figure sent to clients at 18:00 the business day before the release) and the quantity (annualised real GDP growth in the advance print, to one decimal) are kept; the seed's research memo filing the desk's tracking method and its premise that the agency froze its inputs are not used: the office's notice states the late bulletin is incorporated, and the decisive step is re-found in how a book-value stock comes to exist
niche: a bank research desk's call, sent to clients at 18:00 the evening before, on a statistics office's advance estimate of June-quarter real GDP growth at an annual rate, built the day after a monthly trade and business stocks bulletin, delayed by a systems outage, gave wholesalers', retailers' and manufacturers' June stocks at book value, with import prices having risen in two legs, in March and in June
stakeholder_role: a commercial bank's research desk economist who files the desk's call on the advance GDP estimate to clients at 18:00 the evening before the release

spine.entity: one month's merchandise exports or imports with one partner country in one SITC division, as the trade and business statistics unit's bulk download carries it
spine.grain: flow x partner country x SITC division x month

world.geography: a fictional English-speaking country of about 7 million with its own dollar (its statistics office, trade and business statistics unit, reserve bank, bank, poll and people are fictional; personas on the British index)
world.org_type: a commercial bank's economics research desk

driver: The decisive quantity is the change over a period in the volume of a stock that each holder reports at what it paid, and because a holder's stock on any date was bought over a holding period of its own, the reported value mixes the prices of the weeks the goods were bought in; read at the reporting month's price, the textbook removal of price gains, a price step inside the holding period reads as a fall in volume, read at the period's average price it reads the other way, and only revaluing each holder's stock at the average price over its own holding period, at both ends of the period, separates volume from price.
driver_concrete: Each industry's end-March and end-June book-value stocks (wholesale, retail and manufacturing, from the trade and business stocks bulletin) are revalued at the average of the industry's price index over the months its stock-to-sales ratio covers before the change in inventory volume is taken, because import prices rose in March and again in June and the stock on hand at each quarter end was partly bought before each rise; deflating at the quarter end's own price index understates the June volume and overstates the March one, and deflating at the quarter's average price does the reverse.
stump: A strong analyst who takes the desk's track for every line the late bulletin does not feed, builds goods exports and imports from it and deflates each industry's end-March and end-June book-value stocks by that month's price index, the textbook removal of holding gains, files a call about half a point under the golden, because the June leg of the import price rise reads as a fall in the volume of stocks that were bought before it.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who takes the desk's track for every line the late bulletin does not feed, reads the bulletin's book-value stocks and the user guide's volume definition correctly and deflates each industry's end-March and end-June stock by that month's price index files a call about half a point under the golden; deflating at each quarter's average price files one about four tenths over it, and only revaluing each stock at its industry's prices over the months its stock-to-sales ratio covers, at both quarter ends, files the golden.
domain_test: The call turns on the volume of business inventory investment in the advance estimate, which national accountants measure by revaluing book-value stocks at the prices of the weeks the goods were bought in over each industry's turnover period (the turnover method behind the inventory valuation adjustment) before differencing; with a hospital's nouns there is no book-valued stock turning over at cost, no producer price path and no annualised volume aggregate built from expenditure lines, so the task stops reading.
layer1: a monthly bulletin delayed by a systems outage and published as a PDF with tables while the unit's data portal was down
the bulletin's revised April and May figures overlapping the portal download's earlier vintage
price indexes on a 2019 base against national accounts volumes at 2025 prices
values in thousands of dollars in the bulk download and in millions in the bulletin and the office's tables
seasonally adjusted stocks and sales beside unadjusted price indexes
the desk tracker's own line labels against the office's component names, and the pilot log's layout change when a line was split in 2024
contributions in percentage points of the previous quarter's GDP beside a headline at a compound annual rate

differentiation.task259: task259 ages reports filed at earlier dates to a reference date by a market movement measured within reporting units; here nothing is aged to a date: a stock's own book value is decomposed into volume and price, the price being the one its holder paid over its own turnover period, at both ends of the quarter
differentiation.task146: task146 is a bank desk's preview of an insurance board's weekly claims count, decided by refiling released at a quarter turn; here the desk calls a national accounts aggregate and the decisive step is the revaluation of book-value stocks

notes: Stump strategy decomposition_attribution: the bulletin's nominal stock movement is split into volume and price, the price basis (each holder's purchase prices over its turnover period) deciding the split.
